title: Customer Name Search
description:
Find all customers whose name **starts with the letter 'A'**.

**Table: customers**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| email | VARCHAR |
| city | VARCHAR |
| country | VARCHAR |

Output columns: `id`, `name`. Order by `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, country VARCHAR); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'alice@example.com', 'New York', 'USA'), (2, 'Bob', 'bob@example.com', 'London', 'UK'), (3, 'Aaron', 'aaron@example.com', 'Chicago', 'USA'), (4, 'Dan', 'dan@example.com', 'Mumbai', 'India'), (5, 'Amy', 'amy@example.com', 'Los Angeles', 'USA');
solution_sql: SELECT id, name FROM customers WHERE name LIKE 'A%' ORDER BY name

test_cases.description: Aaron, Alice, and Amy start with A

hints: LIKE 'A%' matches any string starting with 'A'. The % wildcard matches zero or more characters.
LIKE '_a%' would match names whose second character is 'a'.
explanation: The `%` wildcard in LIKE patterns matches any sequence of characters. `'A%'` means: start with A, followed by anything. Aaron, Alice, and Amy all qualify.
